neighbours.label: verbs of proving or justifying under a burden of proof: 'must demonstrate that', 'has to prove that', 'show how', 'justify'
fire: To get the permit, the builder must demonstrate that the wall can survive an earthquake.
Under the contract, the seller has to prove that the goods were delivered on time.
The school district will need to show how the new funds improved reading scores.
Each candidate is required to justify the budget in a short written statement.
In court, the plaintiff must prove that the injury was caused by the faulty ladder.
Before approval, the drug maker must demonstrate that the vaccine is safe for children.
The ministry was asked to show that the contracts had been awarded fairly.
Researchers must justify every animal experiment to the ethics board in writing.
quiet: At the fair, the chef will demonstrate a quick way to fillet a salmon.
Leave the bread dough to prove in a warm place for about an hour.
The museum guide showed the children a model of the solar system.
My neighbour explained the rules of cricket to me over a long lunch.
Nobody knows why the old clock in the hall stopped working last night.
The builder showed us the new kitchen before the paint was dry.
The magician performed the trick with the rope twice for the crowd.
During the trial, the jury heard the witness talk about the night of the crash.

notes: Probe: must demonstrate that 0.61, have to prove that 0.57, show how [funds were spent] 0.61, justify their answers 0.52; explain why only 0.17; demonstrate a technique 0.04, explained the recipe 0.03, showed its phone 0.03, tell me why 0.05. The sense of proving a claim matters, not the verb form.
